websiteHeroSubtitle: Klartxt analyses four aspects of a website's privacy behaviour. Here is what each one means and why it matters.
websiteHeroImageAlt: Laptop mockup showing the Klartxt browser extension in use
websiteVideoCaption: Video: Klartxt Privacy Explained, generated with NotebookLM (Gemini), Google LLC, 14 June 2026.
website_tracker_s1_body: Think of trackers like digital shadows. They are tiny, invisible scripts or pixels running in the background of a website. They quietly note which pages you visit, what you click on, and even where you're browsing from.
website_tracker_s2_body: Advertising networks use this information to build a very detailed profile of your interests and habits over time. This data is often traded between companies to show you targeted ads.
website_tracker_s3_body: When a page loads, Klartxt listens carefully to which requests your browser sends out. Each of these requests is checked against a known list of trackers (the DuckDuckGo Tracker Radar) to see who is watching you.
website_tracker_cat_ads_desc: These trackers collect information about you to later show you exactly the right ads.
website_tracker_cat_tracking_desc: They measure how you use the page, sometimes going as far as recording your entire session.
website_tracker_cat_session_desc: These tools record every mouse click, movement and keystroke to replay your session exactly.
website_tracker_cat_content_desc: These are built-in extras like YouTube videos or social media buttons, which often come with their own trackers.
website_tracker_cat_security_desc: These tools protect the site from fraud (for example bots) and usually don't actively monitor you.
website_tracker_cat_functional_desc: Little helpers responsible for additional features like a help chat or payment processing.
website_cookies_s1_body: Cookies are small text files that a website stores in your browser. Like a little sticky note, they help the site remember you. There are good cookies that keep you logged in, and tracking cookies that follow you across different websites to build a profile about you.
website_cookies_s2_body: First-party cookies come directly from the website you are currently on. They are mostly there to make the site usable for you. Third-party cookies come from external companies whose services (like ads or maps) are built into the page. It's like a stranger in a shop making a note about you to recognise you later in a completely different store. They are the main tool for cross-site tracking.
website_cookies_s3_body: Klartxt checks which of these sticky notes are being set, where they come from, and whether they may have already been placed without your permission.
website_cookies_cat_tracking_desc: These cookies follow you from website to website to find out what you like and recognise you.
website_cookies_cat_functional_desc: These sticky notes remember your preferences, for example which language you prefer.
website_cookies_cat_necessary_desc: These cookies are the glue of the website. Without them, features like the shopping cart or login wouldn't work.
website_privacyPolicy_subtitle: The small print for your data
website_privacyPolicy_s1_body: In this document, a website must disclose what happens to your data: what information is collected, why it is done, and who else gets to see it. It's all about transparency.
website_privacyPolicy_s2_body: Laws like the GDPR (European Union, 2016) require that you must be clearly and understandably informed about what happens to your personal information before it is collected.
website_privacyPolicy_s3_body: Klartxt automatically searches the page for a link to this document. If no link is found in the typical areas (like the menu or the bottom of the page), this indicates a possible transparency issue.
privacyPage_overview_body: Klartxt is a browser extension that analyzes specific tracking mechanisms (network requests and cookies) on a website in real time and visualizes them in a structured way. It checks for compliance with the European data protection regulations, identifies data flows, and provides well-founded recommendations for action based on technical analysis.
privacyPage_dataCollection_body: Klartxt does not collect, transmit, sell, or share any personal data. No user data is sent to external servers.
privacyPage_localProcessing_body: All analysis is performed locally within the browser. Detected information (such as trackers, scripts, or URLs) is stored temporarily in session storage and is automatically cleared when the browser tab is closed.
privacyPage_permissions_intro: The extension requires certain browser permissions solely to detect tracking mechanisms:
privacyPage_permissions_network: Network requests are analyzed to identify tracking behavior
privacyPage_permissions_tabs: Tabs are used to associate detected trackers with the correct browser tab
privacyPage_permissions_storage: Storage is used for temporary, session-based data storage
privacyPage_permissions_cookies: Cookies may be inspected for tracking-related purposes only
privacyPage_permissions_sidepanel: Sidepanel is used to display tracking information alongside the current page
privacyPage_permissions_outro: These permissions are not used to monitor user activity or browsing behavior.
privacyPage_noThirdParty_analytics: Klartxt does not use analytics services
privacyPage_noThirdParty_remoteCode: Klartxt does not load remote code
privacyPage_changes_body: If this privacy policy changes, updates will be published in this repository.
imprintPage_disclaimer_body: Klartxt is a browser extension developed as part of an academic project. It is provided as-is without any warranty. The analysis results are based on technical detection and do not constitute legal advice.
imprintPage_project_body: Klartxt was developed as a Bachelor Major Project at SAE Institute Switzerland. The extension is open source and intended for educational and research purposes.
sourcesPage_intro: All sources used in the development of the extension and website are listed below.
